protocol.title: Sensitive Detection and Quantification of SARS-CoV-2 in Saliva
protocol.platform: Saliva-based nucleic acid testing pipeline (RT-PCR + ddPCR); BSL3 RNA extraction, BSL1 analysis
protocol.objective: Validate saliva as an alternative specimen for sensitive SARS-CoV-2 detection using RT-PCR and ddPCR, benchmarked against EUA-certified nasal swab testing by a CLIA-certified clinical microbiology laboratory (CML)

saliva.method: Self-collection by drool technique (spitting into sterile tube to 2 mL line)
saliva.stabilisation: 2 mL Zymo DNA/RNA Shield (ZymoR1100-50) added immediately at collection
saliva.transport: To BSL3 facility for RNA extraction

nasal_swab.method: Anterior nares nasal swab (NS) collected by research team
nasal_swab.clinical_analysis: CML using FDA-EUA Cepheid Xpert Xpress (targets N2 + E gene; positive if Ct < 45 for either)

rna_extraction.primary_method: TRIzol-based RNA extraction (TRE); 17% relative efficiency vs QVK
rna_extraction.glycogen: 1 uL co-precipitant for improved pellet recovery at low RNA concentrations
alternative_kits_evaluated: QIAmp MinElute Virus DNA/RNA Spin Kit (QVDRK)

rt_pcr.master_mix: TaqPath One-Step RT-PCR Master Mix (Thermo Fisher Scientific)
rt_pcr.probe_primer_sets: IDT 2019-nCoV CDC EUA (#10006770): N1, N2, RnaseP
rt_pcr.precision_blue_dye: Precision Blue Real-Time PCR Dye (Bio-Rad), 0.1 uL per reaction
rt_pcr.negative_control: Millipore nuclease-free water processed with RNA extraction methods
rt_pcr.instrument: CFX384 Touch Real-time PCR Detection System (Bio-Rad)

ddpcr.supermix: One-step ddPCR Supermix (Bio-Rad), 5 uL per reaction
ddpcr.probe_primer_sets: IDT (#10006770): N1, N2, RnaseP (same as RT-PCR)
ddpcr.droplet_generator: Bio-Rad QX200 (manual or automated); ~20,000 nanoliter-sized droplets per reaction

steps.name: Saliva specimen receipt
steps.notes: 1 mL aliquot of pre-stabilised saliva (already combined with Zymo DNA/RNA Shield at collection) enters TRIzol extraction protocol. BioScript `dispense` abstracts receipt of specimen into the extraction workflow.

steps.name: TRIzol LS addition
steps.notes: 3 mL TRIzol LS added to 1 mL sample (saliva or nasal swab per paper Methods). Brief vortexing to homogenise. Guanidinium thiocyanate denatures proteins and protects RNA from RNases.

steps.name: Chloroform addition and phase emulsification
steps.notes: 0.6 mL chloroform added; brief vortexing creates water-in-organic emulsion for phase separation. Chloroform separates RNA (aqueous upper phase) from protein and DNA (organic/interphase lower phases).

steps.name: Phase separation centrifugation
steps.notes: Centrifuge 15 min at 12,000xg, 4 C. Three phases form: (1) colourless upper aqueous phase (RNA), (2) white interphase (DNA/protein), (3) red-pink organic phase (protein/lipid). BioScript `heat at 4c for 15m` abstracts centrifugation (no native primitive in BioScript).

steps.name: Aqueous phase transfer and RNA precipitation setup
steps.notes: 0.8 mL colourless upper aqueous phase carefully transferred to new tube (avoid interphase). 1 mL isopropanol and 1 uL glycogen added. Glycogen acts as co-precipitant to improve RNA pellet visibility and yield at low concentrations. BioScript `mix` abstracts manual transfer and addition.

steps.name: Overnight RNA precipitation at -20 C
steps.notes: Paper states 'kept at -20 C overnight or at room temperature for 10 min.' Cold path encoded (higher yield). BioScript encodes as `heat at 4c for 720m` (43200 s in IR). Negative temperatures not tested with lilott8/BioScript compiler; 4 C used as functional cold abstraction.

steps.name: RNA pellet collection centrifugation
steps.notes: Centrifuge 10 min at 12,000xg, 4 C to pellet RNA. Supernatant discarded. BioScript `heat at 4c for 10m` (600 s in IR).

steps.name: 75% ethanol wash
steps.notes: 2 mL 75% ethanol added to pellet; vortexed to wash away residual isopropanol and salts. Salivary fluids are known PCR inhibitors (paper ref. 14: Ochert et al., PCR Methods Appl. 1994). Ethanol wash removes inhibitory substances.

steps.name: Ethanol wash centrifugation
steps.notes: Centrifuge 5 min at 7500g, 4 C to re-pellet RNA. Supernatant discarded. BioScript `heat at 4c for 5m` (300 s in IR).

steps.name: Ethanol evaporation
steps.notes: Pellet air-dried at room temperature for 5-10 min to evaporate residual ethanol. Over-drying reduces solubility; under-drying causes ethanol carry-over PCR inhibition. Upper bound (10 min) encoded. BioScript `heat at 25c for 10m` (600 s in IR).

steps.name: RNA resuspension and QC
steps.qc_module: ddPCR_RnaseP_Detection (used as proxy for Qubit fluorometric QC)
steps.notes: Pellet resuspended in 50 uL RNase-free water. Quantity and quality assessed by Qubit RNA HS Kit. BioScript models Qubit QC as a detect step using the RnaseP module as a proxy for RNA integrity. rnaQcMix disposed after detection; rnaExtract used in downstream PCR steps.

steps.name: RT-PCR reaction assembly (N1, N2, RnaseP channels)
steps.notes: Three parallel RT-PCR reactions assembled targeting N1, N2, and RnaseP (internal control). Serial dilution of SARS-CoV-2 RNA Standard run alongside each plate as positive control. BioScript `dispense SalivaSpecimen` (x3) models aliquoting from the same RNA extract into three separate reactions. Assembly sequence: masterMix + primerSet (5s) -> add RT dye (5s) -> add RNA aliquot (10s).

steps.name: RT-PCR thermocycling (CFX384 Touch, Bio-Rad)
steps.notes: 45-cycle PCR amplification compressed into single `heat at 55c for 45m` block (2700 s in IR). This is a standard BioScript thermocycler abstraction: the compiler has no cycle-loop primitive; each isothermal stage is emitted as a separate heat instruction. Same pattern used in moazami reference file (heat-shock stages encoded as discrete heat calls).

steps.name: RT-PCR fluorescence readout and positive calling
steps.positive_calling_rule: Ct < 40 for N1 OR N2 (CDC recommendation; same threshold for saliva and NS)

channels.FAM: N1 and N2 TaqMan probes (SARS-CoV-2 targets)

steps.notes: N1 used as primary gate (stronger LOD). BioScript does not support compound OR conditionals in a single if statement; N1 is primary signal per CDC positive-calling logic (positive if N1 OR N2 < 40). RnaseP result not used in QC gate but encoded for completeness.

steps.name: ddPCR reaction assembly (N1, N2, RnaseP channels)
steps.notes: Same IDT probe/primer sets (#10006770) as RT-PCR. Three parallel reactions targeting N1, N2, and RnaseP assembled from the same RNA extract. BioScript `dispense SalivaSpecimen` (x3) models aliquoting. Assembly sequence: supermix + RT/DTT (5s) -> add primer set (5s) -> add RNA aliquot (10s).

steps.name: Droplet generation (~20,000 droplets per reaction)
steps.oil: Bio-Rad ddPCR droplet generation oil for probes (#1863005)
steps.notes: Each assembled reaction fractionated into ~20,000 nanoliter-sized droplets at the QX200 droplet generator. Each droplet contains zero or one target RNA molecule, enabling absolute digital quantification without standard curve. `mix ddPCR_rxn with DropletGeneratorOil for 2m` abstracts emulsification at droplet generator.

steps.name: ddPCR thermocycling (C-1000 thermal cycler, Bio-Rad)

performance.dilution_series_lod: N1 target detected at 1:1,000,000 dilution in pool of negatives (Supplementary Table 1)
performance.inhibitor_resistance: ddPCR concentrates targets in smaller reactions, reducing bias from salivary PCR inhibitors (refs 20-22)

steps.notes: 4 C hold encoded as `heat at 4c for 60m` (3600 s in IR); paper protocol allows overnight hold. 45-cycle PCR compressed to single heat block at 55 C (2700 s). Ramping speed 2.5 C/s applied between all stages.

steps.name: Droplet reading and positive calling (QX200, Quantasoft)
steps.positive_calling_rule_NS: CN/uL > 0.1 AND > 2 positive droplets for N1 OR N2 (Bio-Rad manufacturer recommendation for nasal swab)
steps.positive_calling_rule_saliva: BOTH CN/uL AND positive droplet count exceed empirical threshold (mean + 2*SD from 45 pre-operative SARS-CoV-2 negative individuals; Supplementary Table 2)
steps.empirical_threshold_derivation: 45 asymptomatic pre-operative participants, all SARS-CoV-2 negative by CML nasal swab; standard formula: mean + 2*SD (Supplementary Fig. 7)

channels.FAM: N1 and N2 TaqMan probes (SARS-CoV-2 targets)

pass.result_curbside: 15/16 CML-positive samples detected (93.75% concordance); 31/92 total positives vs 16/92 by CML NS assay (Fig. 2e,f)

steps.reproducibility: Independent re-test of 46 saliva specimens (19 positive, 27 negative) confirmed 91.3% concordance (Supplementary Fig. 8). RNA degradation after ~5 months storage explains 4 discordant samples.
steps.notes: N1 used as primary QC gate (LOD 0.06 CN/uL vs N2 at 0.21 CN/uL). ddPCR identified 15 more positives than CML NS assay (curbside cohort), especially at low viral copy numbers (black circles, Fig. 2b). Viral load range spans 10^6-fold across patients (Supplementary Table 4); supercarriers defined as >10,000 CN/mL.

basic_blocks.label: main
basic_blocks.content: TRIzol RNA extraction (S1-S11) + RT-PCR assembly and thermocycle (S12-S14) + ddPCR assembly and thermocycle (S15-S17)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_4_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose RT-PCR signals; ddPCR reaction assembly + droplet generation + thermocycle + readout (S15-S18)

basic_blocks.label: bsbbif_7_j
basic_blocks.content: dispose(ddPCR_N1_Signal, ddPCR_N2_Signal, ddPCR_RnaseP_Signal, rnaQcSignal, rnaExtract); NOP

cfg.cfg_shape: Diamond-diamond (two sequential QC gates, each with true/false branches converging at a join node)

results_summary.saliva_distribution: More uniform viral load distribution vs nasal swabs (less operator variability in collection volume)
